author: @techNmak
title_or_hook: KV Cache explainer: why inference memory is not the weights
summary: A complete, correct-in-structure explainer of the central memory trade-off in LLM serving: KV caching stores per-token key/value vectors per layer per head for the whole sequence; the cache can exceed the weights' memory; it grows with context length and multiplies with concurrent requests; grouped-query attention, KV quantization, and paged KV caching are the named mitigations; and decoding still pays a memory-bandwidth cost reading the cached history, so parameter count alone does not predict serving memory. A teaching text, not a product; no numbers are measured in the post. Feed row 24; video 0:57 attached, the text carries the full argument.
